subject: Intermittent queueing and high tail latency — Weatherly Labs
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ops@weatherly.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent queueing / high tail latency - Weatherly Labs (May 2)

Hi Ben / Marissa,

We saw repeated spikes in per-request tail latency this morning between ~08:45–09:30 PDT where our inference queues backed up and responses stalled for up to 22s (normally < 300ms). This affected ~4% of user-facing requests for ~45 minutes.

Observations:  
- Spike correlates with a batch of high-concurrency nightly jobs kicking off at 08:40.  
- Request patterns show short prompts but many concurrent starts (bursty fan-out).
- Traces attached (weatherly-trace-20260502.json) — includes a few full request/response samples and timestamps.

Can Redwood help triage? Two asks:  
1) Can you confirm whether autoscaler warmed new reserved nodes for our Dedicated pool during that window?  
2) We’re happy to join a quick call and share additional logs and a tokenized sample.

This is impacting user experience; if there are recommended mitigations (e.g., temporary concurrency limits, targeted warmup), we can implement immediately.

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds
SRE Lead, Weatherly Labs
[Attachment: weatherly-trace-20260502.json (application/json)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ops@weatherly.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent queueing / high tail latency - Weatherly Labs (May 2)

Ava — thanks for the report and the trace. We’re investigating now. Quick answers up-front:  
- We saw allocator contention in the same time window for your reserved pool; autoscaler observed pressure but some warm nodes failed to attach within the expected warmup window.
- We’ll prioritize a short triage call so we can collect any missing artifacts and coordinate a replay.

Proposed next steps:  
1) Triage call today (I’m available 11:30–12:30 PDT). If that doesn’t work, we’ll do a working session Mon morning (May 4).
2) Please attach a small tokenized prompt sample and a representative job id (or timestamp range) for the requests in your trace.
3) We’ll produce allocator logs and an initial evidence bundle (allocator-logs-20260502.tar.gz) and share a replay plan.

We’ll also propose a short credit to account for the degraded window while we investigate. I’m looping Rishi and Marissa (engineering & customer ops) to own the fix and coordination.

Ben
Senior Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: placeholder — will provide allocator logs after internal triage]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ops@weatherly.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent queueing / high tail latency - Weatherly Labs (May 2)

Ava — following an internal investigation with infra, here are our preliminary findings and an ask list:  

Preliminary observations (internal):
- Autoscaler received a burst and issued warmup requests; however, the placement allocator returned delayed allocations for ~30% of warm requests due to a transient region-level quota rebalancing.
- Several nodes that marked `WARMING` never transitioned to `READY` within the expected 60–90s window because a placement lease update was delayed by controller-side backpressure. This produced queueing backpressure and elevated tail latency.

Immediate mitigations we can perform with your go-ahead:
1) Replay targeted subset of your traffic in a rehearsal environment during a 2-hour window to validate warmup behavior (we propose Mon, May 4 09:00–11:00 PDT).  
2) Apply a temporary concurrency cap for the job group that triggered the burst (you control the cap).  
3) We’ll ship a hotfix to the allocator to speed lease renewals and force stale warming nodes to re-evaluate (low-risk, can be rolled back).

Data we need from you to scope the replay:
- Representative tokenized prompt file (redacted OK) 
- Job ID(s) or exact timestamp range to isolate traffic 
- Permission to collect anonymized request headers/latency metrics for the timestamps in question

We’ve prepared an initial evidence bundle and notes (initial-rca-notes-20260503.pdf) and a replay plan draft (replay-plan-20260504.md). If you approve the rehearsal, we’ll run the replay in close collaboration and capture traces to confirm the fix.

As Ben mentioned, we’ll apply a credit covering the affected window once we confirm root cause. We’re treating this with high priority — Rishi will coordinate the allocator fix and I’ll own the replay coordination.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial-rca-notes-20260503.pdf]
From: Ava Reynolds <ops@weatherly.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent queueing / high tail latency - Weatherly Labs (May 2)

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick triage and proposed plan. We’re comfortable with the May 4 rehearsal window (09:00–11:00 PDT). A few clarifications and requests:  

- We will provide a redacted tokenized prompt sample and job IDs by 12:00 PDT today. Expect a small file (app-token-sample.txt) with tokenized lines.
- Please confirm data handling: we need to know which fields you will collect and that no PII leaves our environment (we’ll redact anything user-identifying).
- We’d like the credit calculation to be transparent; can you share the proposed credit amount and how it’s computed?

Also, can you include legal/finance on the credit confirmation (cc’ing finance@weatherly.io) and provide the replay plan link so our engineering lead can review before the rehearsal?

Happy to join a pre-replay 20-minute sync at 08:45 PDT.

Thanks,
Ava Reynolds
SRE Lead, Weatherly Labs
[Attachment: app-token-sample.txt (text/plain) — to follow]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ops@weatherly.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, finance@weatherly.io
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent queueing / high tail latency - Weatherly Labs (May 2)

Ava — recap from today’s rehearsal & next steps:  

Summary of actions performed (May 4 rehearsal 09:00–11:00 PDT):
- We ran a targeted replay of your submitted tokenized samples against a staging copy of your reserved pool.  
- Observed the same warmup transition delays in staging; after applying the allocator hotfix (shorter lease re-evaluation and a forced WARMING->RESTART), warm nodes consistently reached READY within ~30s and queued time dropped to baseline.
- We collected allocator logs and perf traces; bundle attached and uploaded to the Drive postmortem link.

Deliverables & timeline:  
1) Evidence bundle: allocator-logs-20260502.tar.gz and perf traces uploaded to https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/postmortems/weatherly-2026-05 (will share direct access).
2) Postmortem doc (draft) link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/postmortems/weatherly-2026-05/postmortem-draft.md
3) Credit: we propose a service credit equal to the pro-rated usage for the affected 45-minute window plus a customer-service goodwill credit. Finance will send formal confirmation to finance@weatherly.io by EOD Tue, May 5.
4) Engineering remediation: hotfix merged to the allocator controller; we’ll deploy to Prod in a staged rollout this week with throttled canaries.

Remaining asks for Weatherly:  
- Confirm receipt of evidence bundle and that the redacted token sample you provided is sufficient for our records.  
- Please sign off on the replay findings and the proposed credit so we can close the incident.

Thanks again for your partnership on this — we’ll follow up with the finalized postmortem and the formal credit paperwork. If you prefer a wrap-up call, we can schedule one tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Senior Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: allocator-logs-20260502.tar.gz, replay-plan-20260504.md]
